existingQuestions.question_text: Under what condition can an officer who has served for less than 10 years qualify for a regular monthly pension from the Military Pensions Board?
existingQuestions.option_a: If he/she is honourably disengaged on medical grounds
existingQuestions.option_b: If he/she holds more than two graduate Certificates earned from a Military Higher Institution of Learning.
existingQuestions.option_c: If he/she has ever participated in a foreign peacekeeping mission for than six months without any break in service.
existingQuestions.option_d: No because ten (10) years is statutorily the minimum period for exiting the Government Service in Nigeria.

existingQuestions.question_text: If a pensioner under PTAD passes away, their Next-of-Kin (NOK) can claim the unpaid balance of their accrued pension assets (arrears) up to the date of death by presenting which legal document?

existingQuestions.option_b: A valid Letter of Administration or Probate Will alongside a Death Certificate
existingQuestions.option_c: A written reference note from the Chairman, Nigerian Union of Pensioners (NUP) for confirmation.
existingQuestions.option_d: A standard passport application slip as a means of identity.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the structural relationship between PTAD and the National Pension Commission (PenCom)?
existingQuestions.option_a: PTAD operates as a commercial subsidiary owned by PenCom.
existingQuestions.option_b: PTAD regulates and inspects PenCom's private PFA accounts.
existingQuestions.option_c: There is no legal or operational interaction between the two agencies.
existingQuestions.option_d: PenCom acts as the supreme regulator that monitors PTAD's compliance with national pension guidelines.

existingQuestions.question_text: For vulnerable, sick, or physically incapacitated pensioners who cannot navigate smartphones for the "I Am Alive" online validation, what alternative operational policy does PTAD provide?
existingQuestions.option_a: Mandatory forfeiture of their monthly stipends, also known as monthly pensions.
existingQuestions.option_b: Specialized mobile field teams that conduct close-quarter home and hospital visits during mobile verification.
existingQuestions.option_c: Forcing the pensioner to travel to the Abuja head office in an ambulance.
existingQuestions.option_d: Transferring the file to a local government ward Office of PTAD for grassroot verification.

existingQuestions.question_text: According to the long-term provisions of the Pension Reform Act, what will happen to PTAD once the last pensioner under the old Defined Benefit Scheme passes away?
existingQuestions.option_a: It will automatically become a private commercial bank in accordance with Oronsaye presidential committee report on the rationalization and restructuring of MDAs.
existingQuestions.option_b: It will be merged with the Ministry of Finance in line with section 997 of Pension Reform Act 2014 (PRA 2014).
existingQuestions.option_c: It will be dissolved, as its transitional mandate will be fully completed as codified in Section 49 of the Pension Reform Act 2014 (PRA 2014).
existingQuestions.option_d: It will begin recruiting young high school graduates into the civil service as directed by PenCom, its regulatory body.

existingQuestions.question_text: To preserve the integrity of the bench, a retired judicial officer drawing a life pension from the CRF is constitutionally barred from which activity?
existingQuestions.option_a: Teaching law at a public university.
existingQuestions.option_b: Appearing or pleading as a legal practitioner before any court of law or tribunal in Nigeria
existingQuestions.option_c: Writing legal textbooks or commentaries
existingQuestions.option_d: Serving as an independent arbitrator in corporate disputes.

existingQuestions.question_text: The harmonized 70-year retirement age and specialized NJC-managed pension protections apply exclusively to judges of:
existingQuestions.option_a: Local Customary Arbitration Panels

existingQuestions.question_text: If a judicial officer is removed from office by the President or a Governor following a recommendation by the NJC for gross misconduct, what happens to his pension rights?

existingQuestions.option_b: He may typically forfeit their right to a statutory life pension.

existingQuestions.question_text: When a judicial officer dies while actively serving on the bench, how are the death benefits and gratuities computed for his Next-of-Kin (NOK)?
existingQuestions.option_a: By counting employee salary deductions over time and pay to all his NoKs enbloc.
existingQuestions.option_b: Using a flat 2 million Naira payment from the Judicial Service Commission.
existingQuestions.option_c: In accordance with public service retirement regulations as statutory charges on the CRF via the NJC

existingQuestions.option_b: His benefits may be reduced, withheld, or forfeited depending on the gravity of the infraction

existingQuestions.option_c: Mainstream commercial court inheritance registries

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the primary statutory length of service required for an employee to qualify for the 100% Exit Benefit Scheme (EBS)?

existingQuestions.option_b: A minimum of 20 years of active public service
existingQuestions.option_c: A minimum of 15 years of continuous service
existingQuestions.option_d: A Minimum of 10 years of active public service

existingQuestions.question_text: Under which of the following circumstances will an officer be granted the EBS before reaching the statutory retirement age or length of service?
existingQuestions.option_a: Voluntary resignation after 3 years of service with proven diligence.
existingQuestions.option_b: Retirement on medical grounds certified by an official Medical Board
existingQuestions.option_c: Transfer of service to a private corporation
existingQuestions.option_d: Proceeding on a self-funded study leave abroad

existingQuestions.question_text: Which of the following conditions automatically disqualifies a retiring officer from being granted the Exit Benefit?
existingQuestions.option_a: Retiring early at the age of 45 years and below
existingQuestions.option_b: Having outstanding liabilities on a government housing loan until later defrayed.
existingQuestions.option_c: Retiring later than 35 years of service
existingQuestions.option_d: Dismissal from the public service on grounds of serious misconduct

existingQuestions.question_text: What condition must an officer with an outstanding government liability (e.g., an unliquidated housing or vehicle loan) meet before their EBS is released?
existingQuestions.option_a: The liability amount is legally deducted from the EBS lump sum before payment.
existingQuestions.option_b: The liability is completely forgiven by the government.
existingQuestions.option_c: The payment is delayed for 10 years until the officer pays out of pocket.
existingQuestions.option_d: The officer must provide a guarantor from the directorate cadre with at least 3 years remaining in service.

existingQuestions.question_text: For an employee's EBS application to be approved by PenCom, what condition must be met regarding their RSA status?
existingQuestions.option_a: The officer must open a separate Retirement Savings Account (RSA) for EBS payment.
existingQuestions.option_b: The officer must reconcile his total contributions on PenCom’s Python Portal.
existingQuestions.option_c: The officer must have contributed a minimum of 15.5 million Naira in his RSA.
existingQuestions.option_d: The officer's RSA must be fully updated and reconciled on PenCom’s COBRA platform.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the primary defining characteristic of the Defined Benefits Scheme (DBS) for Nigerian civil servants?
existingQuestions.option_a: Pension payouts fluctuate entirely based on stock market performance.
existingQuestions.option_b: Employees are required to contribute equally with their employers
existingQuestions.option_c: Retirement benefits are based on the employee's final salary and length of service, funded entirely from the government’s yearly approved budget.
existingQuestions.option_d: Employees contribute 8% of their monthly salary into individual Retirement Savings Accounts (RSAs).

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the old Defined Benefits Scheme, what were the two main financial entitlements given to a retiring civil servant?
existingQuestions.option_a: Terminal resettlement allowance and severance benefits.
existingQuestions.option_b: Retirement Savings Account balance and accrued rights
existingQuestions.option_c: Contributory pension and lump-sum exit benefit
existingQuestions.option_d: Gratuity and monthly pension

existingQuestions.option_a: Civil servants with less than three years to retire
existingQuestions.option_b: Expatriate staff
existingQuestions.option_c: Only political office holders
existingQuestions.option_d: Junior civil servants on Grade Levels 01–06

existingQuestions.option_a: The DBS only covered military and other uniformed personnel

existingQuestions.option_c: The DBS relied on government budgetary allocations, leading to unsustainable pension deficits, unpaid arrears, and massive fraud

existingQuestions.option_b: Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
existingQuestions.option_c: National Pension Commission (PenCom)

existingQuestions.question_text: In what year did the Federal Government of Nigeria officially enact the landmark Pension Reform Act that abolished the old Defined Benefits Scheme for new entrants and introduced the Contributory Pension Scheme?
Under the old public service rules guiding retirement, what is the mandatory retirement age for a civil servant in Nigeria?
existingQuestions.option_a: 70 years old

existingQuestions.option_c: 60 years old

existingQuestions.option_d: 10 years

existingQuestions.question_text: What does the term "Accrued Pension Rights" refer to in the context of the transition from the old scheme to the new Contributory Pension Scheme?
existingQuestions.option_a: The pension benefits an employee earned under the old Defined Benefits Scheme before the commencement of the new scheme
existingQuestions.option_b: The lump-sum payment given upon employment
existingQuestions.option_c: Insurance payouts for injured civil servants who had four (4) years in service before the introduction of the Contributory Pension Scheme.
existingQuestions.option_d: Contributions made by the employer to an overseas account

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the fundamental funding structure of the Defined Benefits Scheme (DBS) for Nigerian Civil Servants?
existingQuestions.option_a: It relies on the individual employee contributing a percentage of their salary monthly into a Retirement Savings Account.
existingQuestions.option_b: It is non-contributory for the employee, and the pension is paid entirely by the government through budgetary allocations.
existingQuestions.option_c: Both the Federal Government and the employee make joint monthly contributions into a centralized fund.
existingQuestions.option_d: Funding is managed by private Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) using employee tax deductions.

existingQuestions.question_text: According to the Nigerian Public Service Rules and pension regulations, what are the statutory conditions for a civil servant to retire with full pension benefits under the DBS?
existingQuestions.option_a: Upon attaining 45 years of age or 15 years of pensionable service, whichever comes first.
existingQuestions.option_b: After completing exactly 10 years of service, regardless of the employee's age.
existingQuestions.option_c: Exactly at 65 years of age, regardless of the number of years spent in service.
existingQuestions.option_d: Upon attaining 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever comes first.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the primary statutory mandate of the Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD)?
existingQuestions.option_a: To manage, administer, and pay pensions to retirees who retired under the Defined Benefits Scheme (DBS).
existingQuestions.option_b: To regulate and license all DBS Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) operating in Nigeria.
existingQuestions.option_c: To prepare all the DBS civil servants for the Contributory Pension Scheme.
existingQuestions.option_d: To invest pension funds in real estate and infrastructural development on behalf of the Federal Government without necessarily waiting for monthly allocations before paying DBS pensioners.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the Defined Benefits Scheme (DBS), who bears the investment risk associated with the payment of pensions?
existingQuestions.option_a: The Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) handling the retiree's account.
existingQuestions.option_b: The Federal Government of Nigeria.
existingQuestions.option_c: The individual retiree through market investments.
existingQuestions.option_d: The National Pension Commission (PenCom).

existingQuestions.question_text: Which specific legislation abolished the old pension schemes in the Nigerian Public Service and established the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), paving the way for PTAD?
existingQuestions.option_a: The Pension Ordinance of 1989 (as amended).
existingQuestions.option_b: The Nigerian Constitution of 1999 (as amended).
existingQuestions.option_c: The Pension Reform Act (PRA), 2004 (later repealed and re-enacted as PRA, 2014).
existingQuestions.option_d: The National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission Act of 1990.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the DBS, how is a retiree's pension typically computed upon retirement from the Nigerian Civil Service?
existingQuestions.option_a: Based on the annual emolument of an employee at retirement and the total qualifying years of service.
existingQuestions.option_b: Based strictly on the total contributions made by the employee and employer over their working years.
existingQuestions.option_c: Based on the average inflation rate over the last five years of active service.
existingQuestions.option_d: A fixed flat rate paid equally to all retirees regardless of rank or years of service.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the name of the periodic biometric verification and validation exercise conducted by PTAD to authenticate DBS pensioners and eliminate 'ghost' pensioners?
existingQuestions.option_a: Integrated Payroll and Personnel Information System (IPPIS) Verification.
existingQuestions.option_b: National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) Enrollment.
existingQuestions.option_c: The Contributory Pension Transition Audit (CPTA).
existingQuestions.option_d: The "I Am Alive" Verification and Confirmation Exercise.

existingQuestions.question_text: Why do DBS pensioners frequently advocate for "Pension Harmonization" in Nigeria?
existingQuestions.option_a: To transfer the payment burden from the Federal Government to private insurance companies.
existingQuestions.option_b: To merge the Defined Benefits Scheme with the Contributory Pension Scheme so everyone receives the same benefits.
existingQuestions.option_c: To ensure that retirees who left service on the same rank and salary grade at different times receive the same pension, irrespective of when they retired.
existingQuestions.option_d: To ensure that all retirees receive their gratuity in a single lump sum rather than installment payments.

existingQuestions.question_text: Which of the following statements accurately contrasts Pension Portability between the DBS and the CPS?
existingQuestions.option_a: DBS allows retirees to transfer their pension benefits to their children, whereas CPS does not.
existingQuestions.option_b: CPS allows the employee to move from one employer to another and maintain the same Retirement Savings Account (RSA), whereas DBS is not portable.
existingQuestions.option_c: Both schemes permit retirees to transfer their accumulated balances to foreign currency accounts upon retirement.
existingQuestions.option_d: DBS pensions are portable, meaning retirees can move from state to federal service and combine their pension records seamlessly.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the Defined Benefits Scheme, how are the funds for pension payments sourced and managed before being disbursed to retirees?
existingQuestions.option_a: The funds are warehoused in a special Central Bank account funded by employer-employee joint contributions.
existingQuestions.option_b: The funds are appropriated annually in the Federal Government budget and released to PTAD for the purpose of paying entitlements of eligible DBS pensioners.
existingQuestions.option_c: The funds are held in individual Retirement Savings Accounts managed by Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs).
existingQuestions.option_d: The funds are raised exclusively through a special Value Added Tax (VAT) dedicated to the payment of qualified Defined Benefits Scheme (DBS) pensioners.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the DBS rules, what is a "gratuity" in the context of a civil servant exiting the service?
existingQuestions.option_a: A penalty fee deducted from a retiree's pension if they retire before the mandatory age.
existingQuestions.option_b: The monthly amount the retiree receives for life after leaving service.
existingQuestions.option_c: A voluntary contribution made by the retiree's colleagues to celebrate their exit from service.
existingQuestions.option_d: A lump-sum tax-free payment made to the retiree upon retirement, distinct from the monthly pension.

existingQuestions.question_text: In comparing the DBS and the CPS, what happens to the Accrued Pension Rights of an active civil servant who was in the DBS before the CPS commenced?
existingQuestions.option_a: The rights are calculated, and the government credits the employee's Retirement Savings Account (RSA) with the bond value.
existingQuestions.option_b: The rights are completely forfeited, and the employee must start saving afresh under the CPS.
existingQuestions.option_c: The rights are converted into shares in government parastatals.
existingQuestions.option_d: The rights are transferred to the Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD) for management until the employee retires.

existingQuestions.question_text: Which of the following represents a major administrative and financial challenge faced by PTAD in managing the Defined Benefits Scheme?
existingQuestions.option_a: Fluctuations in the global price of crude oil have no effect on government funding for PTAD.
existingQuestions.option_b: The existence of unverified or fraudulent pensioners still (ghost pensioners) on the payroll.
existingQuestions.option_c: Disagreements with Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) over the investment of DBS funds.
existingQuestions.option_d: Difficulty in calculating returns on investment for DBS retirees.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), what is the current minimum statutory contribution rate required from both the employer and the employee?
existingQuestions.option_a: A minimum of 10% by the employer and 8% by the employee.
existingQuestions.option_b: 10% by the employer and 5% by the employee.
existingQuestions.option_c: 7. 5% by the employer and 7.5% by the employee.
existingQuestions.option_d: 15% by the employer and 5% by the employee.

existingQuestions.option_a: The National Pension Commission (PenCom).

existingQuestions.option_c: The Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (OAGF).
existingQuestions.option_d: The Ministry of Labour and Productivity.

existingQuestions.option_a: December, 1999
existingQuestions.option_b: October, 2022
existingQuestions.option_d: April, 2023.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the primary statutory function of the National Pension Commission (PenCom) as established by the Pension Reform Act?
existingQuestions.option_a: To independently and directly handle the Retirement Savings Accounts (RSAs) of all civil servants.
existingQuestions.option_b: To regulate, supervise, and ensure the effective administration of pension matters in Nigeria.
existingQuestions.option_c: To serve as the sole custodian of all pension fund assets in the country.
existingQuestions.option_d: To determine the retirement age for all public sector workers.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) governed by the Pension Reform Act, what is the minimum statutory contribution rate for the employer, calculated on the employee's monthly emolument?
What is the minimum statutory rate of contribution expected from an employee under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS)? [1, 2]
Which of the following entities is legally responsible for holding the pension fund assets in safe custody under the Contributory Pension Scheme?
existingQuestions.option_a: Pension Fund Administrator (PFA)
existingQuestions.option_b: Pension Transitional Arrangement Directorate (PTAD.

existingQuestions.option_b: Pension Fund Administrator (PFA)

existingQuestions.option_c: 6 months
existingQuestions.option_d: 3 months.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the minimum coverage required for the Group Life Insurance Policy that employers are mandated to maintain for their employees under the Pension Reform Act?
existingQuestions.option_a: 100% of the employee's annual total emolument
existingQuestions.option_b: 200% of the employee's annual total emolument
existingQuestions.option_c: 300% of the employee's annual total emolument
existingQuestions.option_d: 400% the employee's annual total emolument

existingQuestions.question_text: Can a civil servant transfer their Retirement Savings Account (RSA) from one Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) to another.

existingQuestions.option_b: Yes, an employee can transfer their RSA from one PFA to another once in a year
existingQuestions.option_c: Yes, as many times as the employee desires within a year because he/she has a statutory right to do that.
existingQuestions.option_d: Yes, but only once in a lifetime.

existingQuestions.question_text: What is the aggregate (total) minimum monthly contribution required under the Contributory Pension Scheme, expressed as a percentage of the employee's monthly emolument?
Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Pension Commission (PenCom)?
existingQuestions.option_a: To regulate the pension industry.
existingQuestions.option_b: To License Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs) and Pension Fund Custodians (PFCS).
existingQuestions.option_c: To pay monthly pension and arrears CPS to retirees on a monthly basis.
existingQuestions.option_d: To investigate complaints and resolving disputes in the pension sector.

existingQuestions.question_text: Upon retirement, what percentage of the total balance in a Retirement Savings Account (RSA) can a retiree withdraw as a lump sum, provided the balance can fund a programmed monthly withdrawal or annuity?

existingQuestions.option_b: Not more than 25%
existingQuestions.option_c: Not more than 30%
existingQuestions.option_d: Such lump sum that PenCom may approve, provided the remaining balance covers at least 50% of the retiree's total monthly pay.

existingQuestions.question_text: Under the Pension Reform Act, can an employer choose to bear the full burden of the pension contributions under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) without deducting from the employee's salary?

existingQuestions.option_c: Keeping pension fund assets in safe custody.
existingQuestions.option_d: Providing information on investment strategies and returns to contributors.

existingQuestions.option_c: . The employer's business license is permanently revoked on the first offense.

existingQuestions.option_b: The President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria.

existingQuestions.option_d: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation.
